Variable glossary — correlates of success analyses

crystal_full_test_contig (n=128, 38 hits)

Published

May 21, 2026

1 Purpose

This document defines every variable available for the correlates-of-success analyses on the crystal_full_test_contig run. For each variable it records: where it comes from, what it measures, what it is correlated with by construction, and whether it is valid to include in Analysis 1 (hit prediction).

A dedicated section at the end (§6) investigates the likely codependencies between variables empirically and recommends which to keep when two variables encode overlapping information.

2 Pipeline overview

Stage 0 — Crystal input pose (fixed)
    ↓  RFDiffusion (64 backbone designs)
Stage 1 — Backbone PDB  →  Rosetta filtering (sc ≥ 0.3)
    ↓  ProteinMPNN (2 sequences per backbone = 128 total)
Stage 2 — Designed sequences  →  Sequence QC
    ↓  Boltz-2 via negsteer
Stage 3a — Cold-start Boltz prediction
    → all 3 seeds pass: representative = initial  [stage: initial]
    → fewer than 3 seeds pass: proceed to steering
Stage 3b — Steering (mutations introduced to improve specificity)
    → no contamination detected in any seed: representative = steered design
                                              [stage: steered]
    → contamination detected: trigger reversion
Stage 3c — Reversion (mutated positions reverted to native)
    → pose_holds: mutations genuine (binding survived reversion)
    → pose_collapses: mutations not genuine (binding collapsed on reversion)
    → new_contamination: reversion introduced new contamination
    [all three: stage = reversion]
    ↓
Stage 4 — Outcome: cross_tier (A / B / C / none)

Key constraint: A variable from stage N is downstream of all stage N−1 variables. Variables within the same stage are co-measured and cannot causally predict one another.

The Rosetta filtering step computes interface metrics on the RFDiffusion backbone using Rosetta-placed sidechains. Its primary purpose is the shape complementarity filter (sc ≥ 0.3); the other metrics are by-products of the same run. Crucially, these sidechains are not the final MPNN-designed sequence — they are Rosetta’s own generic rotamer placements on the backbone. This limits the validity of sidechain-dependent metrics such as packing quality and H-bond satisfaction.

All Boltz metrics come from a single Boltz-2 run per design. They are co-measured and cannot causally predict one another.

3 Data

Code 
import sys, warnings, json
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display

HPC_BASE = Path("/Volumes/HPC-Home/receptor_design/receptor-resurfacing-pipeline"
                "/experiments/campaigns/pikp1_avrpikf/runs")
base = HPC_BASE / "crystal_full_test_contig/results"

neg  = pd.read_csv(base / "negative_steering/cross_sequence_summary.csv")
neg  = neg[neg["row_type"] == "steered"].copy()
neg["design_idx"] = neg["source_passing_summary"].str.extract(r"design_(\d+)_seq")[0].astype(float)
neg["seq_idx"]    = neg["source_passing_summary"].str.extract(r"seq_(\d+)/")[0].astype(float)
meta = pd.read_csv(base / "sequences/scored_metadata.csv")
rf   = pd.DataFrame(json.load(open(base / "rosetta_filtering/rosetta_filter_metrics.json"))["designs"])
rf["design_idx"] = rf["design_stem"].str.extract(r"design_(\d+)")[0].astype(float)

df = (neg.merge(meta, left_on=["design_idx","seq_idx"], right_on=["design","seq"],
                how="left", suffixes=("_neg",""))
         .merge(rf, on="design_idx", how="left"))
df.drop(columns=[c for c in df.columns if c.endswith("_neg")], inplace=True)

# Derived variables
lo, hi = df["dG_separated"].quantile([0.01, 0.99])
df["dG_separated_win"] = df["dG_separated"].clip(lo, hi)
df["loop1_len"]        = df["design_region_length_observed"].str.split("|").str[0].astype(float)
df["num_changes_loop"] = df["num_changes"].astype(str).str.split("|").str[0].astype(float)
df["num_changes_tail"] = df["num_changes"].astype(str).str.split("|").str[1].astype(float)
df["mpnn_dr_ratio"]    = df["design_region_score"] / df["mpnn_score"].replace(0, np.nan)
df["hit"]              = df["cross_tier"].isin(["A","B","C"]).astype(int)

HYDROPHOBIC = set("VILMFYW"); POSITIVE = set("KR"); NEGATIVE = set("DE"); AROMATIC = set("FYW")
def aa_f(seq):
    if not seq or pd.isna(seq): return {}
    n = len(seq)
    return {"loop_hydrophob_frac": sum(c in HYDROPHOBIC for c in seq)/n,
            "loop_net_charge":     sum(c in POSITIVE for c in seq)-sum(c in NEGATIVE for c in seq),
            "loop_has_proline":    int("P" in seq),
            "loop_aromatic_frac":  sum(c in AROMATIC for c in seq)/n}
for k,v in df["designed_residues"].str.split("|").str[0].apply(aa_f).apply(pd.Series).items():
    df[k] = v

# Pipeline stage (three categories)
_REVERSION = {"pose_holds", "pose_collapses", "new_contamination"}
df["rep_stage"] = df.apply(
    lambda r: "initial" if r["rep_design"] == "initial"
              else ("reversion" if r["rep_outcome"] in _REVERSION else "steered"), axis=1)

stage_hit = df.groupby("rep_stage")["hit"].agg(["sum","count","mean"]).rename(
    columns={"sum":"hits","count":"n","mean":"hit_rate"})
stage_hit["hit_rate"] = (stage_hit["hit_rate"] * 100).round(1).astype(str) + "%"

print(f"Dataset: {len(df)} designs, {df['hit'].sum()} hits ({df['hit'].mean()*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"\nHit rate by pipeline stage of representative:")
display(stage_hit)
Dataset: 128 designs, 38 hits (29.7%)

Hit rate by pipeline stage of representative:
hits n hit_rate
rep_stage
initial 22 22 100.0%
reversion 14 45 31.1%
steered 2 61 3.3%

The initial stage has a 100% hit rate because cold-start only uses the initial prediction as the representative when all 3 seeds passed the negsteer threshold. It is therefore selected by construction from the highest-confidence predictions — not a surprising result.

The steered stage has a low hit rate, but this is also unsurprising once the logic is considered. Reversion is only triggered when contamination is detected — and contamination can only occur if the target is correctly placed at the true interface (because contamination checks whether mutations at contact positions affect binding). Designs where steering runs but reversion is not triggered are those where the target was never correctly placed to begin with. The binder may have been steered to avoid a scrambled receptor at a different interface entirely, with 6 mutations used to achieve that — and if the target is not at the correct interface, such a design has little chance of being a hit. The steered population therefore contains many designs where Boltz never placed the effector correctly, and the low hit rate reflects this rather than any problem with the number of mutations per se.

The more interesting question — and a candidate for a future analysis — is what determines whether Boltz-2 places the target correctly in the first place, since this appears to be the primary gate before any downstream filtering is useful.

4 Variables by pipeline stage

4.1 Stage 1 — Rosetta filtering

The Rosetta run at this stage places its own generic sidechains on the RFDiffusion backbone and computes interface metrics. These are properties of the backbone geometry, not the MPNN-designed sequence. Metrics that depend on sidechain quality are unreliable here: packstat is 0.000 for every design (confirmed below), and delta_unsatHbonds is computed on Rosetta’s generic rotamers rather than the final sequence.

Code 
rosetta_cols = ["sc_value","dG_separated","dSASA_int","dG_dSASA_density",
                "packstat","delta_unsatHbonds","nres_int"]
print("Rosetta metric value ranges:")
for col in rosetta_cols:
    v = pd.to_numeric(rf[col], errors="coerce")
    unique = v.nunique()
    flag = " ← CONSTANT" if unique == 1 else ""
    print(f"  {col:25s}  min={v.min():8.3f}  max={v.max():8.3f}  "
          f"std={v.std():7.3f}  n_unique={unique}{flag}")

4.3 Stage 3 — Boltz-2 structural predictions

All of the following are co-measured from a single Boltz-2 run. They are downstream of both the backbone and the MPNN-designed sequence. Including them alongside Boltz metrics for hit prediction is valid for understanding which Boltz quality metrics characterise successful designs, but they cannot be used to predict hits before Boltz is run.

4.3.1 Structural confidence metrics

Code

6 Investigating likely codependencies

This section empirically tests relationships between variables that are likely to be redundant. For each group, a correlation matrix is shown and a recommendation made for which variable to retain.

6.1 num_changes_loop vs loop1_len

Question: Is num_changes_loop an independent measure of how much the designed sequence diverges from native, or is it simply a proxy for loop length?

ProteinMPNN rarely reproduces native residue identities in the design region because the RFDiffusion-generated backbone has different local geometry from the native protein — MPNN optimises for the new backbone rather than recovering the original sequence context. If sequence recovery is near-zero for all designs regardless of loop length, then num_changes_loop carries no information beyond the loop length itself.

Code 
seq_recovery = (1 - df["num_changes_loop"] / df["loop1_len"]).mean() * 100
r_loop = np.corrcoef(df["loop1_len"], df["num_changes_loop"])[0, 1]

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))

axes[0].scatter(df["loop1_len"], df["num_changes_loop"], alpha=0.5, s=20, color="steelblue")
axes[0].set_xlabel("loop1_len (residues)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("num_changes_loop")
axes[0].set_title(f"loop1_len vs num_changes_loop\nr = {r_loop:.4f}")
axes[0].plot([df.loop1_len.min(), df.loop1_len.max()],
             [df.loop1_len.min(), df.loop1_len.max()], 'r--', alpha=0.5, label="y=x")
axes[0].legend()

axes[1].hist(1 - df["num_changes_loop"] / df["loop1_len"], bins=20,
             color="steelblue", edgecolor="white")
axes[1].set_xlabel("Sequence recovery (fraction)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("Count")
axes[1].set_title(f"Loop sequence recovery\nmean = {seq_recovery:.1f}%")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print(f"Correlation: r = {r_loop:.4f}")
print(f"Mean sequence recovery: {seq_recovery:.1f}%")
print(f"Max sequence recovery: {(1 - df.num_changes_loop / df.loop1_len).max()*100:.1f}%")

Correlation: r = 0.8373
Mean sequence recovery: 12.4%
Max sequence recovery: 46.2%

Result: r = {r_loop:.4f}. Mean loop sequence recovery is {seq_recovery:.1f}% — confirming that MPNN almost never reproduces a native residue in the design region. num_changes_loop is effectively the same variable as loop1_len and is excluded from all analyses in favour of loop1_len.

6.2 Rosetta metric redundancies

Question: Which Rosetta metrics carry independent information, and which are redundant?

Code 
r_cols = ["sc_value","dG_separated","dSASA_int","dG_dSASA_density",
          "delta_unsatHbonds","nres_int"]
r_corr = rf[r_cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").corr().round(3)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
im = ax.imshow(r_corr.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-1, vmax=1)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(r_cols))); ax.set_xticklabels(r_cols, rotation=40, ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(r_cols))); ax.set_yticklabels(r_cols, fontsize=8)
for i in range(len(r_cols)):
    for j in range(len(r_cols)):
        v = r_corr.values[i, j]
        if not np.isnan(v):
            ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7,
                    color="white" if abs(v) > 0.7 else "black")
plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
ax.set_title("Rosetta metric correlations")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Findings:

  • dG_separated_win and dG_dSASA_density: r = 0.999 — exclude one. dG_separated_win is retained as the more interpretable raw quantity.
  • dSASA_int and nres_int: r = 0.842 — highly correlated. Retain dSASA_int as the continuous measure; exclude the count nres_int.
  • sc_value: |r| < 0.10 with all other Rosetta metrics — entirely independent signal. Retain.
  • delta_unsatHbonds: moderate correlations with dSASA_int (0.498) and dG_separated_win (0.436). Partially independent, but computed on non-native rotamers; treat as uncertain.

Recommendation: Retain sc_value, dSASA_int. Retain delta_unsatHbonds tentatively. Exclude dG_dSASA_density, nres_int, packstat.

6.3 Boltz confidence metric redundancies

Question: Among the Boltz confidence metrics, which carry independent information?

Code 
b_cols = ["rep_iptm_median","rep_ptm_median","rep_interface_plddt_median",
          "rep_ipae_median","rep_pae_pass_frac_median",
          "rep_independent_receptor_rmsd_median","rep_independent_effector_rmsd_median"]
b_corr = df[b_cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").corr().round(3)
short = ["iptm","ptm","iface_plddt","ipae","pae_pass","recep_rmsd","eff_rmsd"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
im = ax.imshow(b_corr.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-1, vmax=1)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(short))); ax.set_xticklabels(short, rotation=40, ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(short))); ax.set_yticklabels(short, fontsize=9)
for i in range(len(short)):
    for j in range(len(short)):
        v = b_corr.values[i, j]
        if not np.isnan(v):
            ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7,
                    color="white" if abs(v) > 0.7 else "black")
plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
ax.set_title("Boltz structural metric correlations")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Findings:

  • iptm, ptm, ipae, pae_pass_frac form a tight cluster: |r| > 0.94 between all pairs. They all measure global complex confidence from the same PAE/pTM outputs — retain iptm only as the most interpretable.
  • interface_plddt: r = 0.779 with iptm — correlated but not redundant. It captures per-residue confidence specifically at the contact surface, which is a distinct aspect from global chain-orientation confidence. Retain.
  • receptor_rmsd and effector_rmsd: r = 0.234 with each other — largely independent. Both retained.

Recommendation: Retain iptm, interface_plddt, receptor_rmsd, effector_rmsd. Exclude ptm, ipae, pae_pass_frac.

6.4 MPNN score redundancies

Question: Do mpnn_score, design_region_score, and mpnn_dr_ratio each carry independent information?

Code 
m_cols = ["mpnn_score","design_region_score","mpnn_dr_ratio"]
m_corr = df[m_cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").corr().round(3)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3))
im = ax.imshow(m_corr.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-1, vmax=1)
ax.set_xticks([0,1,2]); ax.set_xticklabels(m_cols, rotation=20, ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax.set_yticks([0,1,2]); ax.set_yticklabels(m_cols, fontsize=9)
for i in range(3):
    for j in range(3):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{m_corr.values[i,j]:.3f}", ha="center", va="center",
                fontsize=9, color="white" if abs(m_corr.values[i,j]) > 0.7 else "black")
plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
ax.set_title("MPNN score correlations")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Findings:

  • mpnn_score and design_region_score: r = 0.775 — correlated but not redundant. mpnn_score reflects the full receptor–binder complex; design_region_score isolates the de novo positions. Both are informative for different questions.
  • mpnn_dr_ratio: r = −0.452 with mpnn_score and 0.205 with design_region_score. It captures how much harder the de novo region is to design relative to the fixed scaffold, which is partially independent. However, being a derived ratio it adds complexity without a clear biological interpretation advantage. Retain tentatively.

Recommendation: Retain mpnn_score and design_region_score. Exclude mpnn_dr_ratio — it is derived from the other two and does not add independent information.

6.5 Contact metric entanglement with composite score

Question: Is rep_wrong_jaccard_median sufficiently independent of the composite score to be used as a predictor of hit outcome?

Code 
wj = pd.to_numeric(df["rep_wrong_jaccard_median"], errors="coerce")
ra = pd.to_numeric(df["rep_ra_eff_vs_truth_median"], errors="coerce")
cs = pd.to_numeric(df["cross_composite_score"], errors="coerce")

mask1 = wj.notna() & ra.notna()
mask2 = wj.notna() & cs.notna()
r_ra  = np.corrcoef(wj[mask1], ra[mask1])[0, 1]
r_cs  = np.corrcoef(wj[mask2], cs[mask2])[0, 1]

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4))
for ax, y, ylabel, r, title in [
    (axes[0], ra[mask1], "ra_eff (lower=better)", r_ra,
     f"wrong_jaccard vs ra_eff\nr = {r_ra:.3f}"),
    (axes[1], cs[mask2], "cross_composite_score", r_cs,
     f"wrong_jaccard vs composite score\nr = {r_cs:.3f}"),
]:
    ax.scatter(wj[y.index], y, alpha=0.4, s=18,
               c=df.loc[y.index, "hit"].map({0: "#aaa", 1: "#E57373"}))
    ax.set_xlabel("rep_wrong_jaccard_median")
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print(f"r(wrong_jaccard, ra_eff) = {r_ra:.3f}")
print(f"r(wrong_jaccard, composite_score) = {r_cs:.3f}")

r(wrong_jaccard, ra_eff) = -0.334
r(wrong_jaccard, composite_score) = 0.341

Result: rep_wrong_jaccard_median is correlated with both ra_eff (r = {r_ra:.3f}) and cross_composite_score (r = {r_cs:.3f}). The positive correlation with composite score is counterintuitive — it arises because designs that make many contacts overall score highly on both wrong and true Jaccard, and the true Jaccard component dominates composite score. Despite not being a direct ingredient of the formula, wrong_jaccard is entangled with the outcome through this contact-size confound and is excluded from Analysis 1.

7 Final recommended feature set
